description: A coordinator must remember which installations, photos, sign-offs, and documents must be completed before specific inspections can legally proceed on site.

user_profile.context: The required sequence is easy to scramble once multiple teams are working in parallel
user_profile.communication_style: Sequence-focused and compliance-aware, wants dependency order made explicit

fact_sheet.fact: The 'Rough-in Electrical Inspection' for Level 14 of the Apex Tower project is scheduled for October 28, 2024.
The internal tracking code for the Level 14 Rough-in Electrical Inspection is 'ELEC-R14-01'.
All low-voltage conduit on Level 14 must be secured every 3 feet with approved J-hooks before the ELEC-R14-01 inspection can be called.
A photographic log of all in-wall junction boxes on Level 14 must be uploaded to the BuildRight Pro system under folder 'ELEC-R14-01 Photos'.
The 'Form 12B - Electrical Conduit Layout' for Level 14 requires a physical signature from Marcus Thorne, the Site Superintendent.
Site Superintendent Marcus Thorne's office is in Site Trailer A, and his direct line is 555-0182.
Jenna Rios is the Project Engineer responsible for compiling the complete inspection readiness package for ELEC-R14-01.
The official document management system for the Apex Tower project is BuildRight Pro, accessible at https://keystone.buildrightpro.com.
The sign-off from Volt Electric's foreman, Sam Chen, must be captured on the 'Subcontractor Completion Form SF-04' within BuildRight Pro.
The 'Slab-on-Grade Concrete Pour Inspection' for the East Wing foundation is coded 'CONC-SG-E-01'.
For inspection CONC-SG-E-01, all under-slab plumbing sleeves must be installed and successfully pressure-tested to 60 PSI for 15 minutes.
Pressure test results for under-slab plumbing must be documented on 'AquaFlow Plumbing Form PT-11' and uploaded to BuildRight Pro.
Rebar placement for the East Wing slab must be photographed with a 12-inch ruler for scale every 10 square meters.
The designated city inspector for all electrical inspections on the Apex Tower project is Frank Miller.
All photographic evidence submitted for inspections must be geo-tagged and timestamped using the 'SiteCam' mobile application, version 2.5.
Daily coordination updates from all trades are posted by 7:00 AM in the '#apex-tower-daily' channel on Slack.
The staging area for the CONC-SG-E-01 concrete pour is located at the site's south gate, Zone S-4.
The 'Fire-stopping Penetration Inspection' for the Level 12 service core is coded 'FIRE-P12-01'.
Before inspection FIRE-P12-01, all penetrations through fire-rated walls must be sealed with Hilti FS-ONE MAX sealant.
A 'Penetration Log' detailing the location, size, and sealant used for each opening on Level 12 must be submitted 48 hours prior to inspection FIRE-P12-01.
The 'Penetration Log' must cross-reference UL system number 'W-L-3135' for all 4-inch sleeved PVC pipe penetrations.
The on-site lead for AquaFlow Plumbing is Maria Garcia, and her mobile number is 555-0199.
Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) for the Hilti FS-ONE MAX sealant must be included in the FIRE-P12-01 documentation package under Tab 4.
The master inspection schedule is maintained as a Gantt chart in ProCore Project Management Suite, under project ID 'APEX-TWR-2023'.
For the ELEC-R14-01 inspection, a continuity test must be performed on all installed ground wires, with results logged on Form EC-08.
The primary document review station for visiting inspectors is located at Workstation #4 in Site Trailer B.
Any deviation from the approved electrical plans requires a 'Request for Information' (RFI) form to be submitted and approved before work is concealed.
Sam Chen, the Volt Electric foreman, is responsible for submitting the final 'As-Built' electrical drawings for Level 14 within 5 days of passing inspection.
The final step before requesting inspection ELEC-R14-01 is for Jenna Rios to complete the 'Internal Readiness Checklist IR-ELEC-01' in BuildRight Pro.
